title: Operator UX: customer VPC approval experiments
content:
Overview

This is a working PRD-style draft capturing small, focused experiments for the operator-facing approval flow when customers connect a customer-managed VPC (private deployment). The primary intent is to evaluate UX heuristics that reduce manual approver load while preserving forensic auditability and meeting our internal compliance expectations.

Why this doc exists
- Existing approval playbooks (see linked artifacts) are policy-heavy and assume manual operator review for most VPC changes. That creates a backlog and poor customer experience.
- We need to prototype lightweight heuristics + telemetry sampling so we can safely reduce full manual review rate from ~100% -> target 30% for low-risk changes, while preserving chain-of-evidence for audits.
- This doc captures experiment designs, signals, logging contract, and a first pass at acceptance criteria and rollout plan.

Primary goals
1) Define a minimal set of signals that can be used to auto-approve low-risk network changes (prefix: allow/deny, BGP route adds, subnet resize, port change, egress policy).
2) Specify the audit-log schema and retention requirements so every auto-approved action still produces an immutable evidence bundle.
3) Design operator UX: how approvals are surfaced, how overrides happen, and how confidence is presented to approvers.
4) Create telemetry-driven sampling to escalate a fraction of auto-approved changes for manual review to ensure continued model validity.

Personas
- Network Operator (Operator): uses the console to approve/deny customer VPC operations. Needs fast triage, clear provenance, and ability to take remediation actions.
- Customer Onboarding Engineer (COE): coordinates with customers for initial handshakes, expects predictable SLA and clear audit artifacts for compliance.
- Compliance Reviewer: late-stage auditor validating that changes followed the documented process and that logs are tamper-evident.

Experiment heuristics (initial candidates)
- Signal set A (conservative): change_type in {route-add, subnet-add}, source_cidr in customer-trusted-ranges, no recent security incidents (past 30d). Auto-approve if all true.
- Signal set B (behavioral): change submitted by pre-validated automation agent + matching attest token + matching host fingerprint -> auto-approve.
- Signal set C (economic): small-scale resource delta (subnet growth < 10 hosts) + within customer quota -> auto-approve.

Confidence scoring
- Each signal is a binary check (pass/fail). Score = weighted sum (0-100). Thresholds: >=85 auto-approve, 50-85 show recommended approval, <50 block for manual. We will tune weights via A/B sampling.

Audit log contract (required fields)
- event_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), actor_type (customer|operator|automation), actor_id, change_summary (short string), change_payload_hash (sha256 hex), pre_state_ref, post_state_ref, approval_decision (auto|manual|override), approval_reason, approver_id (if manual), evidence_bundle_url (signed URL), retention_policy_tag.
- Note: evidence_bundle must include signed attestations: admin-assertion, automation-token, network-capture-snapshot (pcap or equivalent metadata).

Operator console UX sketches (textual)
- Inbox view: prioritized list sorted by risk_score (descending), with quick filters (auto-approved, recommended, requires-manual). For auto-approved entries show small badge: "Auto-approved (telemetry-verified)" with link to evidence bundle.
- Review panel: 3-column layout (Change summary, Evidence snapshots, Quick actions). Quick actions: re-open, rollback, escalate to SecOps. Each action must create an immutable audit record and send a web-hook to customer contact.
- Override flow: operator can mark "re-open for review" with canned reasons. Re-open triggers immediate rollback template if requested and flags customer SLA.

Telemetry sampling plan
- Week 0–2: 100% manual review on a mirror queue (no customer-visible change) to collect labeled data and tune heuristics.
- Week 3–6: 70% auto-approve low-risk, 30% routed to manual review. Randomized sampling within low-risk bucket; require manual review for 100% of medium/high-risk.
- Ongoing: Rolling calibration weekly. Produce metrics: auto-approval precision, false positives requiring rollback, operator override rate, mean time to remediation.

Acceptance criteria (for graduating an heuristic to production)
- Precision >= 98% on auto-approved changes over at least 1000 events OR false rollback rate <= 0.5% sustained for 4 weeks.
- Audit evidence availability: evidence bundle generated within 30s of change completion, checksum verified, retention tag set.
- Operator satisfaction: median review time for 'recommended' items < 60s in pilot cohorts.

Security & compliance notes
- Evidence bundles must be signed (HSM-backed key in our control plane) and retained per customer's requested retention (default 365 days).
- Tamper detection: maintain merkle-rooted change log snapshots pushed to our immutable ledger and optionally to customer-owned append-only storage (S3/GCS).

Open questions / risks
- Legal: can we auto-approve any changes for customers in regulated industries? Need legal sign-off + per-customer gate.
- Customer opt-in: some customers may require 100% manual sign-off; default behavior should be conservative opt-out rather than opt-in.
- Performance: evidence bundle generation (pcap + attestations) may add latency; need to measure 95th percentile generation time.

Next steps (short-term roadmap)
- Build mirrored queue collector (ENG-PIPELINE) to capture labeled events (week 1). Owner: Diego.
- Implement minimal audit-log schema and storage API; must support signed bundles (week 2). Owner: Maya.
- Console mockups and operator walkthrough sessions (week 2–3). Owner: Liam + UX.
- Pilot with 2 customers on Dedicated tier with explicit opt-in (week 4–6). Owner: Priya + SE.

Appendix: quick checklist for pilot readiness
- [ ] Evidence bundle signing key provisioned
- [ ] Mirror collector running with retention = 90d
- [ ] Operator inbox prototype wired to telemetry
- [ ] Escalation webhooks implemented (customer contact + SecOps)
- [ ] Legal checklist cleared for pilot customers

Notes-to-self / brainstorming fragments
- We could include an "explainability" widget that shows which signals contributed to auto-approval (helps operator trust).
- Consider a rate-limit on auto-approvals per-customer per-hour to avoid mass-change fast-fail scenarios.
- Long-term: allow customers to pin their own approval policy map (explicit allow-lists) stored in their attestation bundle.

Questions for next sync
- UX session invite: who should be in the room? Recommend: 1 operator, 1 SE, 1 legal, 1 eng infra.
- Can SRE provision ephemeral forensic snapshot storage for the pilot?
